replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
Mr Driver, Ms Rider — here is what the record decides, and why.

The $4.00 no-show fee can stand only if all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, and the driver's side must carry every one of them.

Limb (a) is met: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 08:12:35. Limb (d) is met: the driver cancelled at 08:20:30 on code EXCESSIVE_WAIT, one of the three codes that limb recognises, with no boarding and no started_at.

Limb (b) fails. POL-NS-02 deems arrival only where the trace holds at least three consecutive fixes, each at 25 m accuracy or better, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius round the pickup pin. The driver's own trace is complete — 93 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps — but its qualifying in-geofence fix count is zero. The nearest raw reading, 37.9 m, would sit inside the radius on its face, but it and every other in-radius reading fail the 25 m filter, so they count as evidence of neither presence nor absence. With no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes before cancellation, POL-NS-02 is explicit: the driver never arrived, limb (b) fails, and the rider gets the fee back. This is a test that ran and found nothing qualifying, not a limb left undecided — POL-NS-08 discloses no clock skew, no gap over 120 seconds, no chat defect and no fare mismatch.

Limb (c) fails too. Dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the 'arrived' tap, so the measured hold is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum — a 300-second shortfall. That is POL-NS-06, and it refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present. The only route that could have lengthened the hold, POL-NS-06(i) interval-summing, is shut: EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), and a missing advisory makes that limb unavailable.

The driver's arguments are answered, not ignored. The trip record's 7.9-minute wait and its arrival marker are the driver's own tap and the app's ETA; POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05 both send the waiting clock to the GPS, not the tap, so the marker cannot manufacture a dwell the trace does not show. For the same reason there is no unresolved conflict for POL-NS-09(b) to escalate — the policy resolves it — and neither the anti-farming check (2 no-show terminations against 132 completed trips, 1.5%, below both POL-NS-07 limbs) nor the repeat-dispute counters fire. That the rider's own 60-fix track is filtered out as well does not help the driver: her presence is not a condition he can defeat, while limbs (b) and (c) are conditions he must establish and has not. The fare line is sound — $4.00 is the greater of the STANDARD zone fee and the RYDE_X tier fee, both $4.00 — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect.

POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied 28 seconds after the rider's locating message, well inside the 120-second window.

Ms Rider, you also ask that a false-arrival record be entered against the driver under POL-NS-05. I decline that. POL-NS-05 fires only where the arrival marker is false — the trace placing the driver more than 300 m out, or moving at 15 km/h or more, at the 08:12:35 timestamp. The trace reports movement across the whole window (mean 294 m, speeds up to 43.5 km/h) and its nearest reading is 37.9 m, inside the radius; it gives no position or speed for that instant. The falsity of the marker is therefore not established and no referral issues. Movement across the window supports the finding that no qualifying dwell exists; it does not meet the separate test for a false marker.

No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full, and POL-NS-03 does not apply because the trace does not show the driver stationary for a full 300 seconds anywhere within 400 m of the pin.

Outcome: the $4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.
